related_questions.question: What to take for a COVID cough?

text_blocks.snippet: For a COVID-19 cough, it's important to determine if it's a wet or dry cough to choose the right treatment. For a wet cough with mucus, expectorants can help loosen and expel the mucus. For a dry cough, cough suppressants can help relieve the urge to cough. Additionally, staying hydrated, soothing the throat with warm drinks, and using cough drops or lozenges can provide relief. If shortness of breath is a concern, slow breathing techniques and relaxation methods may be helpful.
snippet_highlighted_words: expectorants can help loosen and expel the mucus

list.title: Expectorants:
list.snippet: These medications help thin and loosen mucus, making it easier to cough up.

list.title: Hydration:
list.snippet: Drinking plenty of fluids, like water or warm beverages, helps thin mucus.

list.title: Warm drinks:
list.snippet: Warm liquids like tea with lemon and honey can soothe the throat and loosen mucus.

list.title: Sipping fluids:
list.snippet: Taking small sips of liquid when you feel the urge to cough can help suppress the cough.
Cough suppressants: These medications help reduce the frequency and intensity of coughing.
Cough drops or lozenges: These can help soothe a sore throat and moisten the mouth and throat.
Hydration: Staying hydrated is still important for a dry cough to help soothe the throat.
Pain relievers: If coughing is painful, acetaminophen can help relieve pain.
Shortness of breath: Slow breathing techniques and relaxation methods can help regulate breathing.
Inhalers: If you have an inhaler prescribed for shortness of breath, use it as directed and disinfect the mouthpiece after each use.
Avoid sharing inhalers: Never use someone else's inhaler.

related_questions.question: How to quickly get rid of COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: There is no guaranteed "quick" way to get rid of COVID-19, as the recovery time varies. However, the primary approach involves rest, over-the-counter medication for symptom relief, and staying hydrated. For those at higher risk of severe illness, early treatment with antiviral medications within a specific timeframe after symptom onset can reduce the risk of hospitalization and death.
snippet_highlighted_words: There is no guaranteed "quick" way to get rid of COVID-19

list.snippet: Rest: Prioritize getting more sleep than usual (7-9 hours or more).
Symptom Management: Over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen can help with fever and body aches, according to UnityPoint Health.
Stay Hydrated: Drink plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration.
Monitor Symptoms: Pay attention to any worsening symptoms and seek medical advice if needed.
Early Treatment: If you are at higher risk, consult with a doctor to discuss antiviral medications, which are most effective when started within 5-7 days of symptom onset.
Isolate and Protect Others: Stay home and avoid contact with others to prevent further spread.
Proper Hygiene: Wash hands frequently and avoid sharing personal items, advises UnityPoint Health.
The body's immune response plays a crucial role in clearing the virus, and recovery time can vary depending on individual factors.
Antiviral medications, if needed, are most effective when started early in the course of the illness, so don't delay seeking medical advice if you are at higher risk.
If you experience a medical emergency, such as difficulty breathing, seek immediate medical attention by calling 911, suggests UnityPoint Health.
